prerequisites: Ability to abstract: translate from colloquial language to mathematical language (and vice versa).
Handle and understand basic mathematical symbology (e.g. summation).
Handle and understand the real function with a real variable.
Apply the concept of derivative and integral in one variable to elementary functions.
Use basic knowledge of the applications of the limit concept of a function.
Transform units from one scale to another.
Contents from Mathematics II or Mathematics applied to Social Sciences in 2nd year of Baccalaureate.
Contents corresponding to Baccalaureate Mathematics subjects.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and aptitudes in the field of Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment and solidarity spirit.
Ability to work in a team.
Search for information through different means. Manage it.
Make decisions.
Plan, organize, and strategize.
Estimate and schedule work.
Be able to use Statistics as a necessary tool in their future professional practice.
Be aware of the degree of subjectivity indicated by the interpretations of statistical results.
Analyze the risk of decisions based on statistical results.
An adequate command of oral and written language is very important to be able to model real problems.
Ability to solve statistical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge of statistics.
Collect statistical data, present it clearly and summarized, and analyze the results.
Make forecasts for different working conditions and estimate their reliability.
Use statistical models in solving real problems.
Make decisions in an uncertain environment.
Manage the different measurement scales and their possibilities in statistical analysis.
Discriminate between the objectives of a statistical analysis: descriptive and inferential.
Distinguish between a statistical population and a sample from it.
Understand the information provided by a statistical table that orders sample data.
Summarize sample information using measures of centralization, dispersion, and position.
Compare information obtained from different samples.
Recognize the degree of dependence between different characteristics of a sample.
Model the dependence between different characteristics of the sample using a function (linear or non-linear). Use the model for prediction. Reliability of the prediction.
Know the probabilistic basis of Statistical Inference.
Assign statistical models to different real-life behaviors. Identify the different distributions.
Use descriptive techniques for classification and obtaining information through characteristic parameters of the analyzed sample or population.
Estimate unknown parameters of a population from a sample.
Manage principles and applications of statistical hypothesis tests.
Compare two populations based on their characteristic and unknown parameters.
Formulate real problems in statistical terms (parameter estimation, hypothesis testing,...) and apply Statistical Inference to their resolution.
Be proficient in the use of tables, calculators, and statistical packages.
Be able to use Statistics as a necessary tool in their future professional practice.

syllabus_topics: Descriptive Statistics: Basic concepts: Population and sample. Parameters and statistics. Frequency distributions. Graphical representations. Measures of central tendency, position, and dispersion. Linear regression and correlation. Other types of regression.

Probability Calculus: Events. Concept of probability and properties. Fundamental theorems in probability: Bayes' Theorem. Random variable. Distribution function. Most common probability models in Engineering, their most important characteristics and applications.

Statistical Inference: Point estimation. Interval estimation: confidence coefficient. Construction of confidence intervals for common parameters. Parametric hypothesis testing: Concepts related to hypothesis testing. Non-parametric tests: Chi-square test, goodness-of-fit to a distribution, independence and homogeneity tests. Normality tests. Inference in regression.
Practical 5: Independence tests and linear correlation.
teaching_methods: Individual study (research, information analysis, manipulation, elaboration)
assessment_rules: For the ordinary and extraordinary (June) calls, the final grade is calculated as 0.7 x EX + 0.2 x PL + 0.1 x EC. In the extraordinary (June) call, taking any test implies implicitly renouncing the corresponding grade from the ordinary call. For the extraordinary (January) call and differentiated assessment, the final grade is calculated as 0.8 x EX + 0.2 x PL, with no continuous assessment component. In all cases, a minimum final grade of 5 out of 10 is required to pass the course. If there is doubt about authorship or unauthorized means, an in-person defense may be requested.
